review_notes: I reviewed all of lines 1–109. The file has one declaration, the theorem `MvPolynomial.rename_quasiFinite_iff`. It adds no definitions, no simp lemmas and no simp-set attributes, so it creates no simp rewrite directions, competing rules or cycles. The proof uses `simp only [Function.Surjective, not_forall, not_exists] at hf` to turn the negated surjectivity hypothesis into `∀ j, ∃ i, ¬ f i = j`-style form. This is a local, terminating use. The three `simp [ψ, ψa, φ, ε, ...]` calls unfold local `let` bindings and use the standard `aeval`, `rename` and `constantCoeff` simp lemmas. They are scoped to the proof and don't show a simp-interface flaw. I did not run Lean, so I can't say whether any of these calls fails or is slow. Making the iff statement `@[simp]` is not justified: its right-hand side is a disjunction with an unrelated `Subsingleton R` side condition, and the file shows no downstream uses that need it. I also did not search the repository for downstream callers, because there was no candidate rule to evaluate.
